This guide is written for the faculty member's administrative
assistant, who is responsible for day-to-day data entry and
record maintenance in the Promotion Review Tracker. The tracker
is a ZZedc application configured to monitor the faculty
member's academic progress across research, teaching, and
service domains in preparation for an upcoming promotion review.
No knowledge of R, databases, or ZZedc internals is required. A
lab data scientist has installed and configured the system; this
guide covers everything the assistant will do day to day.

This revision (last verified 2026-10-31, against the EDC tab as
actually run and clicked through in a browser) corrects several
claims in the previous version of this guide that described an
intended future design rather than the application's actual
current behavior. Where a tab does not yet do what you might
expect, that is noted explicitly below rather than left implied.

---

## 1. Launching the Application

Open a terminal or RStudio console and run:

```{r}
library(zzedc)
launch_zzedc()
```

The application opens in your default browser. By default it
picks a free port automatically, so the exact address (something
like `http://127.0.0.1:XXXXX`) is printed to the console when it
starts -- it is not always the same address twice. If your lab
data scientist has configured a fixed, memorable address for you,
use that instead and ignore the console output. Keep the console
open while you work; closing it stops the server.

If you prefer a persistent local installation that starts
automatically, ask the lab data scientist to configure
auto-launch on login.

---

## 2. Logging In

Click the **EDC** tab in the top navigation bar. If you are not
already logged in, a login box appears over the page. Enter your
username and password there and click **Login** (or **Dismiss**
to close the box without logging in).

The application does not force a password change on first login;
if the lab data scientist issued you a temporary password, ask
them to generate a permanent one for you, or follow their
instructions for changing it yourself. Choose a password you will
remember; it is not recoverable without the lab data scientist's
help, since only a hash of it is stored.

---

## 3. Application Layout

Once logged in, the **EDC** tab shows three sections side by side:

- **Left:** your username and a **Form** dropdown. This is how
  you switch between the seven tracking domains -- there is one
  combined data-entry screen, not seven separate tabs.
- **Middle:** the fields for whichever form is currently selected,
  with a **Submit entry** button below them.
- **Right:** a panel (currently labeled "Messages" in the
  interface -- this is a cosmetic leftover, not a messaging
  feature) listing the five most recent entries *for the
  currently selected form only*, with search and paging controls.

The top navigation bar also has **Home**, **Reports**, **Data
Explorer**, and **Export** tabs. As of this writing, those four
do not yet reflect your real tracked data -- see Section 5 below
before relying on any of them.

---

## 4. Entering Data

### How to create a new entry

1. Click the **EDC** tab, then choose the relevant form from the
   **Form** dropdown on the left.
2. Assign a tracking ID following the convention for that domain
   (see each section below).
3. Fill in the fields. Required fields are marked with a red
   asterisk. A field with a fixed list of options (Status, Term,
   Role, and similar) is presented as a dropdown you choose from,
   rather than free text.
4. Click **Submit entry**. A green "Entry saved." banner appears
   on success and the entry immediately appears in the recent-
   entries panel on the right. If a required field was left
   blank, or an entered value is not one of a field's listed
   options, a red notification describes the problem and the
   entry is not saved; you can keep editing and resubmit.

### Editing an existing entry

The EDC tab does not currently support reopening a saved entry
for editing. If something was entered incorrectly, note the
tracking ID and ask your lab data scientist to correct it
directly in the database; do not try to work around this by
submitting a duplicate corrected entry under the same tracking
ID, since tracking IDs are not enforced as unique.

---

### 4.1 Publications (`PUB-YYYY-NNN`)

Use this form (listed as "MANUSCRIPTS Form" in the Form dropdown)
to track every manuscript from initial concept through
publication. Create one record per manuscript.

**Tracking ID convention:** `PUB-2026-001`, `PUB-2026-002`, ...
Reset the counter each calendar year. This is a convention for
you to follow consistently; the application does not check or
enforce the format.

| Field | What to enter |
|---|---|
| Tracking ID | Unique identifier, format `PUB-YYYY-NNN` |
| Manuscript Title | Working or final manuscript title |
| Target Journal | Journal of intended submission |
| Co-authors | Comma-separated list of co-author surnames |
| Status | Current stage, chosen from the dropdown below |
| Submission Date | Date the manuscript was first submitted |
| Acceptance Date | Date of formal acceptance notice |
| Publication Date | Date of online or print publication |
| DOI | Digital object identifier once assigned |
| Notes | Any notes relevant to the promotion dossier |

**Status options** (choose one from the dropdown):

- `ideation` -- concept stage, not yet drafted
- `drafting` -- active writing in progress
- `submitted` -- submitted to a journal, awaiting desk decision
- `under_review` -- sent to external reviewers
- `revision` -- revision requested; manuscript in progress
- `accepted` -- accepted; in production queue
- `in_press` -- accepted and assigned a DOI; not yet in an issue
- `published` -- assigned to a volume and issue

The three date fields are plain date pickers; the application
does **not** currently check that they are in a sensible order
(e.g. it will accept an acceptance date before the submission
date without complaint). Double-check the dates yourself before
submitting.

**Tip:** enter a record at ideation stage and update the status
field as the manuscript progresses by submitting a corrected
entry (see "Editing an existing entry" above for the current
limitation on this).

---

### 4.2 Courses (`CRS-YYYY-NNN`)

Use this form ("COURSES Form" in the dropdown) to record every
course you developed or taught. One record per course per term.

**Tracking ID convention:** `CRS-2026-001`, `CRS-2026-002`, ...

| Field | What to enter |
|---|---|
| Tracking ID | Unique identifier |
| Course Code | Department code and number, e.g., `FMPH 101` |
| Course Title | Full course title |
| Academic Year | e.g., `2025-2026` |
| Term | Fall, Winter, Spring, or Summer (dropdown) |
| Role | `developed`, `taught`, or `developed_and_taught` (dropdown) |
| Student Count | Total enrolled students |
| Contact Hours | Total instructor contact hours for the term |
| Notes | Curriculum innovations, guest lectures, etc. |

**Contact hours** are the total hours you spent in scheduled
instructional contact with the class, not preparation time.
A three-credit lecture course meeting three times per week for
ten weeks is 30 contact hours.

---

### 4.3 Mentoring (`MNT-YYYY-NNN`)

Use this form ("MENTORING Form" in the dropdown) to record
individual tutorial relationships. One record per student.

**Tracking ID convention:** `MNT-2026-001`, `MNT-2026-002`, ...

| Field | What to enter |
|---|---|
| Tracking ID | Unique identifier |
| Student Initials | Initials only (e.g., `J.D.`) |
| Student Level | undergraduate, graduate, postdoc, or other (dropdown) |
| Start Date | Date the relationship began |
| End Date | Date the relationship ended (leave blank if ongoing) |
| Hours per Week | Approximate weekly tutorial hours |
| Topic Area | Research area or skill being mentored |
| Outcome | Degree earned, publication, employment, etc. |
| Notes | Any notes relevant to the dossier |

As with Publications, the application does not currently check
that the end date falls on or after the start date -- check this
yourself.

---

### 4.4 Grant Reviews (`GNT-YYYY-NNN`)

Use this form ("GRANT_REVIEWS Form" in the dropdown) to record
each external grant review service. One record per review
assignment.

**Tracking ID convention:** `GNT-2026-001`, `GNT-2026-002`, ...

| Field | What to enter |
|---|---|
| Tracking ID | Unique identifier |
| Agency | Funding agency, e.g., `NIH`, `NSF`, `PCORI` |
| Program Name | Study section or program name |
| Panel Name | Panel or review group identifier |
| Review Date | Date of the review panel meeting or deadline |
| Role | `reviewer`, `chair`, or `observer` (dropdown) |
| Notes | Notes relevant to the dossier |

---

### 4.5 Committees (`COM-YYYY-NNN`)

Use this form ("COMMITTEES Form" in the dropdown) to record
standing or ad-hoc committee memberships. One record per
committee.

**Tracking ID convention:** `COM-2026-001`, `COM-2026-002`, ...

| Field | What to enter |
|---|---|
| Tracking ID | Unique identifier |
| Committee Name | Official name of the committee |
| Organization | Institution or body, e.g., `UCSD`, `ASA`, `NIH` |
| Scope | departmental, institutional, national, or international (dropdown) |
| Role | Your role, e.g., `member`, `chair`, `secretary` |
| Start Date | Date your membership began |
| End Date | Date your membership ended (leave blank if current) |
| Meeting Frequency | Typical meeting cadence (dropdown) |
| Active | `yes` if membership is current, `no` if completed (dropdown) |
| Notes | Notes relevant to the dossier |

The end-date-after-start-date check described for Mentoring above
does not apply here either; verify manually.

---

### 4.6 Journal Reviews (`JRV-YYYY-NNN`)

Use this form ("JOURNAL_REVIEWS Form" in the dropdown) to record
each peer review assignment. One record per manuscript reviewed.

**Tracking ID convention:** `JRV-2026-001`, `JRV-2026-002`, ...

| Field | What to enter |
|---|---|
| Tracking ID | Unique identifier |
| Journal Name | Name of the journal |
| Manuscript ID | Blinded identifier supplied by the journal |
| Review Date | Date you submitted your review |
| Recommendation | Your editorial recommendation (dropdown) |
| Notes | Notes relevant to the dossier (do not include manuscript details) |

**Recommendation options:** `accept`, `minor_revision`,
`major_revision`, `reject`, `not_reviewed`.

Use `not_reviewed` if you declined after seeing the abstract.
This maintains a complete record of all review requests.

---

### 4.7 DSMB Memberships (`DSB-YYYY-NNN`)

Use this form ("DSMB Form" in the dropdown) to record data safety
monitoring board memberships. One record per trial.

**Tracking ID convention:** `DSB-2026-001`, `DSB-2026-002`, ...

| Field | What to enter |
|---|---|
| Tracking ID | Unique identifier |
| Trial Name | Abbreviated or full trial name |
| Sponsor | Funding agency or industry sponsor |
| Role | `member`, `chair`, `statistician`, or `other` (dropdown) |
| Start Date | Date your membership began |
| End Date | Date your membership ended (leave blank if current) |
| Meeting Frequency | Typical meeting cadence (dropdown) |
| Active | `yes` if membership is current, `no` if completed (dropdown) |
| Notes | Notes relevant to the dossier |

---

## 5. Reviewing, Reporting on, and Exporting Your Data

**As of this writing, the Data Explorer, Reports, and Export
tabs in the top navigation bar do not read your real tracked
entries.** They were built as general-purpose demonstration
screens and still show synthetic sample content (random numbers,
placeholder statistics like "87% complete", and generic
columns such as "Patient Demographics" that have nothing to do
with this tracker). This is a known gap, tracked separately from
the EDC data-entry screen itself, which *does* read and write
your real data correctly.

Concretely:

- **Data Explorer** shows a randomly generated 50-row sample
  table, not your manuscripts, courses, or other entries.
- **Reports** (Basic Report, Quality Report, Statistical Report
  under the Reports menu) show a demo histogram of random
  numbers and hardcoded placeholder statistics, not summaries of
  your actual data.
- **Export** offers export options for data sources ("Patient
  Demographics", "Adverse Events", etc.) that do not correspond
  to anything in this tracker; do not use it to produce dossier
  files yet.

**Until this is fixed**, the only verified way to see your real
data is the recent-entries panel on the right side of the EDC
tab, which lists up to five of the most recent entries for the
currently selected form. For anything beyond that -- a full
pipeline view, a count by status, or an export for the promotion
dossier -- ask your lab data scientist to query the database
directly on your behalf.

---

## 6. Recommended Data Entry Cadence

Keeping the tracker current takes roughly five to ten minutes per
entry if done at the time the activity occurs. Batch
reconstruction is error-prone.

| Activity | When to enter or update |
|---|---|
| New manuscript | At conception (status: `ideation`) |
| Manuscript submission | Same day (new corrected entry noting submission date) |
| Manuscript accepted | Same day (new corrected entry noting acceptance date) |
| Manuscript published | Same day (new corrected entry noting DOI, publication date) |
| Course taught | First week of each term |
| Mentoring relationship | At start and end |
| Grant review completed | Same day as review deadline or panel meeting |
| Committee meeting attended | End of each semester |
| Journal review submitted | Same day |
| DSMB meeting attended | Day of the meeting |

Because the EDC tab cannot currently reopen a saved entry for
editing (Section 4), "update" above means asking your lab data
scientist to make the correction directly, or -- if you and your
department are comfortable with duplicate tracking IDs for the
same manuscript at different stages -- submitting a new entry.
Confirm your department's preference before choosing an approach.

---

## 7. Troubleshooting

**The application will not launch.** Close the browser and
re-run `launch_zzedc()` in a fresh R session. The console prints
the address to open; if nothing prints, ask your lab data
scientist to check for a startup error.

**A save fails with a validation error.** Read the red
notification; it identifies the field and what is wrong. The
most common causes are a required field left empty, or (rarely,
since most constrained fields are dropdowns) a value that is not
one of a field's listed options.

**A record is missing.** Records are not deleted from the
database; if it was saved, it is there. The recent-entries panel
on the EDC tab only shows the five latest entries for the
currently selected form, so an older record will not appear
there -- ask your lab data scientist to look it up directly
until the Data Explorer tab is wired to real data (Section 5).

**You forgot your password.** Contact the lab data scientist.
Passwords are hashed and cannot be recovered, but an
administrator can reset the account.

---

## 8. Glossary

- **Tracking ID**: the unique identifier you assign to each
  entry. Follow the domain prefix conventions in Section 4. Not
  currently enforced to be unique by the application.
- **Status**: the current lifecycle stage of a manuscript, chosen
  from a fixed dropdown list.
- **Contact hours**: total scheduled instructor-student contact
  time for a course, not including preparation.
- **Form dropdown**: the selector on the left of the EDC tab used
  to switch between the seven tracking domains.
- **Recent-entries panel**: the list on the right of the EDC tab,
  currently labeled "Messages" in the interface, showing the five
  most recently saved entries for the currently selected form.
